q: The notion of incremental stability (δ-ISS or incremental input-output stability) strengthens stability by requiring the system to be stable with respect to differences between trajectories. A system is incrementally stable if:
opts: Any two solutions x(t,x₀,u) and x(t,x₀',u') satisfy |x(t,x₀,u) − x(t,x₀',u')| ≤ β(|x₀−x₀'|,t) + γ(||u−u'||)
The system has a unique equilibrium
exp: Incremental stability: δ-ISS means the difference between any two solutions satisfies a KL+K gain bound in the differences of initial conditions and inputs. This is stronger than ordinary stability and ensures uniqueness of steady states and convergence of trajectories to each other — crucial for observer design and synchronization.
